title: Reserve Breaks Down
note: Overwhelmed by longing, she can’t hold back what she should keep to herself, and lets it out. Reserve means others don’t learn your secrets. It fails because she spoke to her heart, so this chapter follows that one.

couplets.plain: The axe of desire breaks down the door of reserve, bolted with modesty.
couplets.pm: The axe of desire is breaking the door of reserve, on which modesty is the bolt. Neither can stand now, and I can’t bear this. While modesty lasts reserve won’t fail, so it is the bolt. Reserve keeps what is inside from others, so it is the door. Both are strong and won’t go of themselves, but her longing removes them together, so it is the axe.
couplets.context: Her friend tells her to bear it, so that her modesty and reserve aren’t lost. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: The axe of desire breaks down the door
links.reason: Desire is the axe no door of reserve withstands, even one bolted with modesty.

couplets.plain: This thing called desire has no mercy. Even in the dead of night it rules my heart and puts it to work.
couplets.pm: Even at midnight, when everyone stops work, it punishes my heart and works it, so the thing called desire has no kindly regard. The work is sending her heart to him. Desire was born in her heart, and putting your mother to work isn’t the way of the world, so she says “a thing called desire”. She means it can’t be held down.
couplets.context: Her friend says desire born in the heart can be held down by the heart. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: This thing called desire has no mercy.
links.reason: Sums up desire in one word, merciless, for the hold it keeps on her heart.

couplets.plain: I would hide my desire, but it comes out without warning, like a sneeze.
couplets.pm: I mean to hide this desire inside me, but what use is that? It breaks out against my will, like a sneeze. It can’t be held in, any more than a sneeze can.
couplets.context: Her friend says women can hide desire. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Desire does not ask leave to show itself, however she tries to keep it in.
A sneeze measures how little the will has to do with desire coming out.

couplets.plain: I used to say I had reserve. Now my desire has gone past hiding, out into the public square.
couplets.pm: Until today I thought I had reserve. What use was that? Today my desire has gone past hiding and come out in the public square, so that many people know it. It is no longer in my power.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: The great dignity of not going after those who hurt you is not something known to people with the sickness of desire.
couplets.pm: The reserve that doesn’t follow those who left, but keeps away from them in turn, is known only to people of pride who don’t have the sickness of desire. She says “hurt” because he makes time that should pass in joy pass in pain. Going after him means thinking of him without a break. My heart goes even to one who doesn’t value it, and I know no other way.
couplets.context: Her friend says they should forget the man who has forgotten them. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: treats running after one who hurt you as natural

links.quote: The great dignity of not going after those who hurt you
links.reason: Names the dignity that won’t go after those who hurt you, then says the sickness of desire has none of it.

couplets.plain: It makes me want to go after the one who hurt me. What a fine thing, this sorrow that has come to me!
couplets.pm: What kind of sorrow has come to me, making me want to go after the one who left me? A very fine one! “Fine” is scorn. She means this sickness of desire can’t be spoken of or listened to, and is utterly cruel.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: When the one we cherish does, in desire, all we long for, we don’t even know there is such a thing as modesty.
couplets.pm: When the man I desired came and, in desire, did what I longed for, we knew nothing at all of modesty. Modesty here is shame at touching a chest that courtesans have touched. What she longed for is the lovemaking her craving had dwelt on. Seeing her own fault in joining him unthinkingly, she says “we”, to include her friend.
couplets.context: He came back from a courtesan, and she lost her reserve and went to him. Her friend asks why she didn’t sulk, and she answers.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Aren’t the humble words of that thief of many tricks the army that breaks down our womanhood?
couplets.pm: The army that destroys the wall of our reserve is the humble talk of this thief, skilled in many lies, so how could it stand? Womanhood here means reserve. I had planned to sulk and not give way, but he came so that it all vanished and I was ahead of him in union. His humble words claim he has more loving-kindness than I do.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: I went off meaning to sulk. I saw my heart was ready to join him, and I embraced him.
couplets.pm: Meaning to sulk when he came, I went off somewhere else and didn’t stand before him. But my heart, with no reserve, betrayed me and began to join him. Seeing that, I knew sulking wouldn’t work, and I embraced him. The heart is the means of sulking, and it had become the means of union.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Can those whose hearts are like fat in a fire say, when they come together, that they will hold to their sulk?
couplets.pm: Fat put in a fire melts, and so do the hearts of women when they see their lovers, and their reserve is gone. When he draws close, can such women think they will sulk and stay that way without relenting? They can’t. Coming together here means coming very near, or meeting. I am such a woman, so sulking wasn’t possible for me.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: hearts are like fat in a fire
links.reason: A heart yields as surely as fat in a fire when the lover draws close.

ideaLinks.quote: The axe of desire breaks down the door of reserve, bolted with modesty
ideaLinks.reason: Desire’s axe breaks the door, and modesty’s bolt gives way with it.

ideaLinks.quote: I went off meaning to sulk. I saw my heart was ready to join him
ideaLinks.reason: Desire leaves no room to sulk: every attempt at it collapses the moment he is near.
